concepts.name: Nucleotide and DNA structure
concepts.summary: Recall that DNA is an antiparallel double helix of nucleotides (sugar, phosphate, base) paired A-T and G-C by hydrogen bonds.

concepts.name: Semiconservative replication
concepts.summary: Describe how each new DNA molecule contains one original strand and one newly made strand, each parental strand serving as a template.

concepts.name: RNA types and differences
concepts.summary: Distinguish RNA from DNA (ribose, uracil, usually single-stranded) and name the roles of mRNA, tRNA and rRNA.

concepts.name: Central dogma flow
concepts.summary: Explain that genetic information is copied from DNA to RNA by transcription and read by ribosomes to make protein by translation.

concepts.name: Codons and genetic code
concepts.summary: Explain that three-base codons specify amino acids, that the code is redundant and nearly universal, and that AUG starts and stop codons end translation.

concepts.name: Purpose of molecular techniques
concepts.summary: Recall what PCR, gel electrophoresis, restriction enzymes and sequencing are used for in general terms.

misconceptions.text: Each new DNA double helix is made entirely of new strands, or the old DNA is kept intact and a fully new copy is made.
Proteins are made directly from DNA in the nucleus without an RNA intermediate.
Each amino acid is specified by exactly one codon.

concepts.name: Replication enzymes and roles
concepts.summary: Explain what helicase, primase, DNA polymerase, topoisomerase and ligase each do at the replication fork.

concepts.name: Leading and lagging strands
concepts.summary: Apply the 5'→3' synthesis rule to predict which strand is made continuously and which as Okazaki fragments.

concepts.name: Transcription stages
concepts.summary: Describe how RNA polymerase binds a promoter, synthesizes RNA from the template strand and terminates.

concepts.name: Eukaryotic mRNA processing
concepts.summary: Describe capping, polyadenylation and removal of introns by splicing to produce mature mRNA.

concepts.name: Using the codon table
concepts.summary: Transcribe a template strand and translate the mRNA into an amino acid sequence, predicting effects of point mutations.

concepts.name: Translation steps with tRNA
concepts.summary: Use codon-anticodon pairing to trace how a ribosome builds a polypeptide from an mRNA.

concepts.name: Gel electrophoresis and restriction digest
concepts.summary: Predict fragment patterns when DNA is cut by restriction enzymes and separated by size on a gel.

concepts.name: PCR cycle steps
concepts.summary: Apply the denaturation, primer annealing and extension cycle to predict the amount of product after n cycles.

misconceptions.text: DNA polymerase can start a new strand from scratch without a primer and can synthesize in either direction.
Introns are the parts of mRNA that are translated and exons are removed.
In gel electrophoresis, larger DNA fragments travel farther than smaller ones.

concepts.name: Replication initiation and origins
concepts.summary: Analyse how origins are recognized and forks assembled, and why bacteria use a single origin while eukaryotes use many.

concepts.name: Proofreading and DNA repair
concepts.summary: Analyse how polymerase proofreading and mismatch repair keep replication error rates low.

concepts.name: Prokaryotic operon regulation
concepts.summary: Predict operon expression under different conditions and mutations using repressors, operators, inducers and activators like CAP.

concepts.name: Eukaryotic transcription factors
concepts.summary: Analyse how general and specific transcription factors, enhancers and chromatin state control gene expression.

concepts.name: Alternative splicing and spliceosome
concepts.summary: Analyse how the spliceosome recognizes splice sites and how alternative splicing yields multiple proteins from one gene.

concepts.name: Plasmid cloning design
concepts.summary: Design a cloning workflow with compatible restriction sites, ligation, transformation and selection using antibiotic resistance and reporters.

concepts.name: PCR primer design and optimization
concepts.summary: Design primers with suitable length, melting temperature and specificity and troubleshoot failed or nonspecific amplification.

concepts.name: Sanger sequencing principle
concepts.summary: Analyse how dideoxynucleotides terminate chains to produce fragments read as a sequence.

misconceptions.text: The lac operon is switched on whenever lactose is present, regardless of glucose levels.
Proofreading eliminates all replication errors so no mutations arise from replication.
Any primer that matches the target will work in PCR regardless of its melting temperature or self-complementarity.

concepts.name: CRISPR-Cas9 mechanism and editing
concepts.summary: Analyse how guide RNA and PAM direct Cas9 cuts and how NHEJ versus HDR determine editing outcomes.

concepts.name: Quantitative PCR and RT-PCR
concepts.summary: Evaluate qPCR designs, controls and Ct data to judge gene expression or template quantity.

concepts.name: Next-generation sequencing workflows
concepts.summary: Analyse library preparation, read alignment and coverage and the trade-offs between short- and long-read methods.

concepts.name: Post-transcriptional regulation
concepts.summary: Analyse how miRNAs, siRNAs and mRNA decay pathways tune gene expression after transcription.

concepts.name: Epigenetic and chromatin control
concepts.summary: Analyse how histone modifications and DNA methylation alter accessibility and transcription.

concepts.name: Expression vectors and protein production
concepts.summary: Evaluate vector, promoter, tag and host choices to express functional recombinant protein.

concepts.name: Experimental controls and troubleshooting
concepts.summary: Judge results from cloning, PCR and gel experiments and diagnose failures using appropriate controls.

misconceptions.text: CRISPR-Cas9 edits are always precise and only happen at the intended target site.
A lower Ct value in qPCR means less starting template.
Epigenetic marks change the DNA sequence itself.

concepts.name: Designing genome editing strategies
concepts.summary: Design editing strategies choosing among nuclease, base and prime editing and plan validation of on- and off-target outcomes.

concepts.name: Evaluating sequencing approaches
concepts.summary: Evaluate which sequencing assay and depth best answers a question about expression, binding or variation, accounting for bias and error.

concepts.name: Synthetic gene circuit design
concepts.summary: Create regulatory circuits from promoters, repressors and RNA elements and predict their dynamics and failure modes.

concepts.name: Mechanistic models of gene regulation
concepts.summary: Evaluate quantitative models of transcription, translation fidelity and noise against experimental data.

concepts.name: Replication-transcription conflicts and genome stability
concepts.summary: Evaluate how collisions, R-loops and stalled forks cause instability and how cells resolve them.

concepts.name: Designing rigorous molecular experiments
concepts.summary: Create experimental plans with orthogonal assays, controls and statistics that distinguish causal mechanisms from artefacts.

concepts.name: Therapeutic nucleic acid strategies
concepts.summary: Evaluate the benefits and risks of ASOs, siRNA, mRNA and gene-editing therapies for a given disease mechanism.

misconceptions.text: Sequencing with high coverage removes all errors and biases from the result.
Engineered gene circuits behave in cells exactly as designed on paper, independent of host context.
Gene expression is a smooth, deterministic process, so average measurements capture cell behaviour.
